query: Turquoise killifish has recently emerged as a powerful new laboratory model to study experimental biology of aging due to its short lifespan and to its wide range of aging-related changes, which include neoplasias (Di Cicco et al., 2011), decreased regenerative capacity (Wendler et al., 2015), cellular senescence (Ahuja et al., 2019; Valenzano et al., 2006), and loss of microbial diversity (Smith et al., 2017).
